title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #617: Balanced Colourings of Complete Graphs**

This problem asks whether a strong uniformity condition on edge colourings of complete graphs can hold. A balanced r-colouring of K_n means every induced K_{r+1} uses all r colours on its edges. The Erdős-Gyárfás conjecture (1999) asserts that no balanced r-colouring of K_{r²+1} exists when r ≥ 3.

**Status:** OPEN in general. Proved for r=3 (K₁₀) and r=4 (K₁₇) by Erdős-Gyárfás. False for r=2 (the Petersen graph complement gives a balanced 2-colouring of K₅).

**Key insight:** The threshold r²+1 is sharp — K_{r²} CAN be balanced for infinitely many r, so the single extra vertex is what forces non-existence.
mathContext: ∀ r ≥ 3, ∀ c : K_{r²+1} → Fin r, ∃ S ⊆ V with |S| = r+1 and some colour missing from edges(S)

title: Graph and Colouring Primitives
content:
**Complete Graph, Edges, and Colourings**

The formalization builds from three primitives:

- **CompleteGraph n:** The complete graph on Fin n, where Adj v w iff v ≠ w
- **Edge n:** An unordered pair {v, w} ⊆ Fin n with card = 2
- **EdgeColouring n r:** A function from edges to Fin r (assigning one of r colours)

These are concrete, computable definitions that work well with Lean's type system. The vertex set Fin n is finite and decidable, making the combinatorial arguments cleaner.
mathContext: K_n on vertex set {0, ..., n-1} with r-coloured edges

title: Colour Coverage in Cliques
content:
**Colours Used in Induced Subgraphs**

The central definitions for the conjecture:

- **InducedClique n k:** A subset S ⊆ Fin n with |S| = k, representing an induced K_k
- **coloursUsed c S:** The set of colours appearing on edges within S (axiomatized)
- **usesAllColours c S:** Every colour in {0,...,r-1} appears on some edge of S
- **missesColour c S:** At least one colour is absent from the edges of S

The coloursUsed function is axiomatized rather than defined computationally because extracting the 2-element subsets of a finset and mapping through the edge type requires substantial finset infrastructure.
mathContext: coloursUsed(c, S) = {c(e) : e ∈ E(K_S)} ⊆ Fin r

title: Balanced and Non-Balanced Colourings
content:
**The Balance Property**

IsBalanced n r c holds when EVERY induced K_{r+1} in K_n uses all r colours. This is an extremely strong uniformity condition — it requires that no matter which r+1 vertices you pick, every colour appears on at least one edge among them.

IsNotBalanced is the negation: there EXISTS some induced K_{r+1} missing at least one colour. The conjecture asserts that IsNotBalanced always holds for K_{r²+1} when r ≥ 3.

title: The Erdős-Gyárfás Conjecture
content:
**Formal Statement of the Conjecture**

ErdosGyarfasConjecture states: for all r ≥ 3, every r-colouring of K_{r²+1} is not balanced. The equivalent formulation ErdosGyarfasEquivalent says: for all r ≥ 3, no balanced r-colouring of K_{r²+1} exists.

The r² + 1 vertex count is crucial — it's the smallest number of vertices where balance should be impossible, since K_{r²} CAN be balanced.

title: Known Cases: r = 3 and r = 4
content:
**Solved Cases (Erdős-Gyárfás 1999)**

The conjecture is proved for r = 3 and r = 4:

- **r = 3:** Every 3-colouring of K₁₀ has a K₄ missing a colour. A K₄ has 6 edges; balance requires each colour to appear exactly twice. The counting argument shows this is impossible across all K₄ subgraphs of K₁₀.

- **r = 4:** Every 4-colouring of K₁₇ has a K₅ missing a colour. A K₅ has 10 edges; the argument is similar but more involved.

The general case r ≥ 5 remains open — the counting arguments become harder to control.
mathContext: r_3_solved : ∀ c, IsNotBalanced 10 3 c; r_4_solved : ∀ c, IsNotBalanced 17 4 c

title: Boundary Cases and Counterexamples
content:
**Why r ≥ 3 and r²+1 Are Both Necessary**

Two counterexamples show the conjecture's hypotheses are tight:

- **r = 2 fails:** The Petersen graph complement provides a balanced 2-colouring of K₅. Every triangle uses both colours, so the balance condition is satisfied. This shows r ≥ 3 is necessary.

- **K_{r²} can be balanced:** For infinitely many r, balanced r-colourings of K_{r²} exist. This shows the +1 in r²+1 is essential — you need that one extra vertex to force non-balance.
mathContext: ∃ balanced 2-colouring of K₅; ∃ r ≥ 3 with balanced r-colouring of K_{r²}

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**Complete Summary of Known Results**

The summary theorem erdos_617_summary bundles the three main known results into a single conjunction:
1. Every 3-colouring of K₁₀ is not balanced (r=3 case)
2. Every 4-colouring of K₁₇ is not balanced (r=4 case)
3. A balanced 2-colouring of K₅ exists (r=2 counterexample)

The general conjecture for r ≥ 5 remains one of the notable open problems in edge-colouring theory.
mathContext: erdos_617_summary : (∀ c, ¬balanced 10 3 c) ∧ (∀ c, ¬balanced 17 4 c) ∧ (∃ c, balanced 5 2 c)
